correctness.rationale: For each pair of evaluation points, the free uniform constant coefficient makes the first evaluation uniform and independent of the difference. The linear coefficients map uniformly onto the principal ideal generated by coordinate differences, and every higher monomial evaluation difference stays inside the same ideal. Hence the exact joint-zero probability is gcd(m,differences)/m^2, including diagonal pairs. Euler totient divisor decomposition and congruence-class counting prove the stated arbitrary-subset covariance and all-modulus second moment identities. Prime-power specialization yields precisely k(1-1/p) in one variable. Reconstructed all boundary cases m>=2,n>=1, any eligible monomials; 5,998 exhaustive coefficient vectors with exact rational arithmetic across 10 models and 2,754 ordered point-pair checks corroborated the formula, but are not used to infer universality.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A finite field of cardinality p^k is not Z/p^kZ and has no zero divisors; the finite-field pairwise independence law does not imply the positive multiscale covariance at composite moduli. Actual p-adic root-count moment theorems do not imply finite-level congruence solution counts, which include singular approximate roots that may not lift.

originality.rationale: The original 2023 Jain--Moon--Wu preprint proves finite-field zero-count laws but explicitly conjectures the finite prime-power expected count and univariate variance (Conjecture 5.7, PDF page 11). The present statement supplies the composite-ring missing moments in every dimension and a stronger all-subsets congruence-class covariance kernel. The 2022 Bhargava--Cremona--Fisher--Gajovic theorem is about actual Q_p-roots; the 2006 Evans theorem is about a p-adic system, not congruence roots. Targeted searches of published records produced no equivalent statement. Priority remains at risk due to unexamined 2025 publisher full text and obscure finite-ring evaluation identities; negative searches are not a proof of absolute priority.
residual_risks: A full-text revised journal article from 2025 was not accessible through the publisher listing; the open arXiv 2023 original was materially read and labels the target as a conjecture.
An earlier equivalent covariance identity in finite-ring polynomial evaluation or coding/statistics literature could be unindexed or phrased differently.
Semantic database retrieval and keyword searches do not establish absolute novelty or independence; this is a self-review only.

value.rationale: The exact variance k(1-1/p) was explicitly conjectured for random univariate polynomials modulo prime powers by Jain--Moon--Wu (2023, Conjecture 5.7). The theorem proves that question without a degree restriction beyond free linear terms, extends it to all composite moduli and dimensions, and gives the full spatial covariance decomposition and covariance of root counts on arbitrary regions. These motivate finite-level congruence root clustering and quantification of uncertainty; neither classical divisor inversion alone nor a finite table provides the stochastic covariance theorem. Does not assert complete distribution stabilization or higher-order association.
